function: Secure multi-beam transmit design for a satellite downlink: DNN mutual-information estimator guides tuning of GMM symbol mapping and beam separation; cross-entropy antenna subsets (p. 5-9).
system: Satellite at 1200 km with two ULA subarrays of 100 antennas each (50 active), single-antenna ground receivers, QPSK; carrier band not stated; no RIS (p. 2-3, 10).
method: DNN conditional-density estimator trained on simulated samples (maximum likelihood) to estimate mutual information; GMM mapping and beam separation tuned by finite-difference gradient descent; cross-entropy antenna selection (p. 5-10).
data_channel: Own simulation: array-response superposition along direction theta plus Gaussian noise, 1200 km altitude geometry; 1000 samples per estimation, 10 eavesdropping points (p. 3-4, 10).
test_conditions: Designed and evaluated in the same simulator over 10 sampled eavesdropping directions; beam pointing errors of 0.3-0.5 degrees; three-subarray case; MI estimator checked on Gaussians (p. 10-13).
baselines: Classical only: antenna weight optimization, symbol-level precoding, random antenna selection, conventional beamforming; no learned baseline (p. 11-13).
metrics: BER, secrecy capacity, average mutual information leakage, insecure-area diameter, maximum side-lobe energy, MI estimation accuracy (p. 10-13).
complexity: Order per iteration: O(H) for the MI estimator, O(KHQ) for symbol-mapping optimization, O(Nc log Nc) for cross-entropy selection; no runtime or parameter counts (p. 6-7, 9).
openness: none: no code or data link; simulation only (p. 10).
q1_support: p. 3: "the noise-free superimposed signal along any arbitrary". The signal is a superposition of ULA array responses plus Gaussian noise, with orbit height, array sizes and QPSK set in Table I (p. 10); no 3GPP TR 38.811, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 12: "We simulate the BER performance under these three error conditions". This is a sweep over beam pointing error, and the three-subarray case is redesigned by the recursive procedure (p. 8, 12); no trained model is tested in a new scenario or dataset.
q3_support: p. 12: "we consider traditional antenna weight optimization [55] and symbol-level precoding schemes [56]". These baselines and the random antenna selection (p. 11) are non-learned; no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 7: "The computational complexity of Algorithm 2 at each iteration is O(KHQ)"; O(H) for the estimator (p. 6) and O(Nc log Nc) for Algorithm 4 (p. 9).
q5_support: p. 10: "we utilize a Gaussian sampler for training the MI estimator". Samples come from the authors' own simulator; no link, DOI, public dataset or measured data is given.
notes: Borderline eligibility, reviewer to confirm. Included because the paper states "A deep learning-based iterative optimizer was then developed to jointly design the signal mapping and beamforming for multiple beams" (p. 13) and trains a DNN estimator (Algorithm 1, p. 6). The transmit parameters are tuned by finite-difference gradient descent (p. 7) and a cross-entropy search, and no learned model is deployed, so if the DNN is read as only a metric estimator the work is no_learning. Area 6: the design controls beams, symbol mapping and power of a satellite downlink; physical-layer security is not among the function exclusions. Table I (p. 10) is image-only and was read from the page image.
